your_book:
Jaleel's book slipped a modest 0.72% on Friday, a broadly defensive session where the damage was spread rather than concentrated. The clearest drag came from Boston Scientific (BSX, –1.7%), which remains in a tough spot: still carrying an elevated risk flag after management slashed FY26 growth guidance to 7–8.5%, and today's price action did nothing to stabilise the –10.4% unrealised loss. Expand Energy (EXE, –2.0%) was Friday's worst single-day performer in percentage terms, adding to an already –7.2% unrealised position. ADBE and ONON each shed roughly 1.5–1.6%, continuing to drift. On the positive side, AstraZeneca (AZN, +1.23%) and Novartis (NVS, +1.32%) both caught a bid — a small irony given the drug-pricing policy overhang flagged across the pharma cluster. NVDA (+0.22%) and ABT (+0.22%) ticked up in line with broad chip and defensive healthcare tone.

The most important divergence in the book right now is between verdict and price trajectory. LULU carries a BUY verdict yet sits –20.8% unrealised with a guidance cut confirmed in June and the next read not until December 9 — that is a long time to wait for a catalyst in a name already under structural margin pressure from tariffs and stalling China sales. BSX is rated STRONG BUY yet is –10.4% with management itself guiding flat through Q3; the thesis and the numbers are moving in opposite directions. RKLB remains rated AVOID at 7.6% weight, which is the single most conspicuous misalignment in the book — a near-top-ten position in a name the model explicitly flags as one to exit.

Watch BSX into its October 28 earnings; any further downward revision to guidance will test whether the STRONG BUY conviction is justified or whether the position needs to be right-sized. The RKLB weight deserves an explicit revisit before then: holding 7.6% in an AVOID-rated name is a capital-preservation concern in its own right. ADBE's narrative-driven slide (AI-moat fears, CFO exit) bears monitoring — the next print is December 9, but the stock can re-rate further on sentiment alone in the interim.

attention.headline: 7.6% weight in an AVOID-rated name
attention.note: RKLB is the sixth-largest position in the book yet carries the sole AVOID verdict and the lowest QARP score (37.4) by a wide margin — this misalignment between size and conviction requires an explicit, documented decision, not drift.
